answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it can trade, then slash that stake when independent counterparties prove collusion or repeated fraud. A trusted inlet of verified observations can anchor those proofs, while a wharf of bonded agents settles disputes; the oasis of cheap, instant identities no longer helps, because multiplying them requires tying up more capital and risks losing it. This raises the attacker’s cost without assuming that one person can have only one account.
